item.title: Using Sonaweft
item.description:
Hear a completed example

Open the completed scientific example to hear a human-voiced NOAA interview about gravity, follow actual recognition text and download a hashed bundle. Prepared listening notes are labeled separately from optional review-provider output. This precomputed example does not start another transcription job.

Upload and inspect

The hosted workflow accepts authorized English audio/video up to 64 MiB and 60 minutes. Upload a file and inspect its duration/quote before confirming work. The hosted application does not download arbitrary platform URLs or use your browser cookies.

item.title: Building Sonaweft: speech, source and recovery
item.description:
Source chronology

The original instascript command and import paths remain compatible. Hosted workbench 7fde01a (owner-access source record) added the upload/review/export workflow. 5ac1d7c added the original completed audio example; handoff 68b8472 (owner-access source record) normalized artifacts and corrected the provider reference. The old optional Claude/vault documents are archives, not required setup.

1. Preserve source and recover work

The standalone CPU CLI uses FFmpeg/FFprobe and faster-whisper. Immutable original recognition, separate corrections, generated notes and sourced questions became distinct artifacts. Private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication support deliberate recovery; cross-path perceptual deduplication is not promised.

item.title: Technical overview
item.description:
Hosted transcription workflow

Sonaweft runs Python/FastAPI, a serialized SQLite ledger and hosted speech workers on Modal behind Cloudflare. Inspect authorized English audio/video up to 64 MiB / 60 minutes before confirming transcription. The eligible free sample transcribes the first thirty seconds, subject to private availability. Completed examples start no inference.

Listen to timestamped segments, keep immutable recognition separate from saved corrections, and optionally consent to transcript-text review by DeepSeek. Audio is not sent to that text provider. Public HTTPS direct media/RSS sources use checked redirects; arbitrary platform pages, private cookies and unrestricted URL downloads are not supported. Recognition, corrections, optional AI notes and scholarly metadata are separate evidence.

item.title: Product contract
item.description:
Source and interpretation stay separate

Sonaweft accepts authorized English recordings, produces timestamped speech recognition, and keeps original text separate from later corrections, speaker-label annotations, optional AI notes and external research candidates. Manual labels do not establish speaker identity; recognition and AI output require review against the recording.

Inspection and quotes precede processing. The bounded sample is subject to private availability. Optional transcript review sends text to the named provider only after consent; audio is not sent to that text provider. Selected-span jobs retain original recording offsets and do not erase older work. Explicit retries use fresh quotes and retained recognition where available.

item.title: Processing architecture
item.description:
Browser --> secure cookie + CSRF --> FastAPI / Modal
 |--> serialized SQLite ledger writer
 |--> private media volume (48-hour TTL)
 |--> confirmed CPU coordinator
 |--> FFmpeg normalization
 |--> L4 / faster-whisper large-v3
 |--> optional DeepSeek text review
 |--> committed result --> settle hold
Review player / separate corrections / portable exports <--|
Explicit selected claim --> Crossref metadata candidates

Isolated checkout --> Paddle --> signed durable inbox
 |--> fresh transaction + all adjustment pages
 |--> intent/owner/product-bound credit or revocation

instascript/contract.py validates original ASR and exact source-quoted review and creates versioned exports. pipeline.py provides local private checkpoints, exclusive locks, completion hashes and atomic publication. review.py bounds text/output, validates JSON and has no autonomous tools. Local source.py downloads are never invoked for public uploads.

item.title: Owner operations
item.description:
Current public operating boundary

Sonaweft runs behind its public Cloudflare gateway on Modal. Email-first signup, verification and mailed resets for verified addresses are deployed alongside private-key recovery. Accounts and balances are product-specific. Google/GitHub owner sign-in/linking acceptance has passed; checkout is closed.

Admission and privacy

Live free processing checks visitor eligibility and private shared availability before dispatch. An unavailable or unverifiable admission check refuses new processing with Currently unavailable. Please try again later. Completed examples remain open. Signing in does not reset sample eligibility.

item.description:
Original record: Release evidence — 15 October 2026.

Sonaweft is deployed at https://m-amir-gomaa--sonaweft-web-app.us-east.modal.run . /health reports hosted processing enabled and billing disabled. Existing Pageweft cloud identities, balances and files were not migrated.

Check Actual evidence Scope
Automated suite 52 tests passed, Python safety lint and both JS syntax checks passed Real temporary SQLite/files/FFprobe; model dispatch and Paddle HTTP are mocked
Local speech Existing cached small model transcribed the original generated recording in about 5.4 seconds CPU/int8 on this laptop; not an accuracy benchmark
Cloud speech Pinned large-v3 revision on Modal L4 returned the expected two English sentences Real inference, cloud-cached weights; not local MX350 inference

Public workflow Chromium uploaded/inspected the generated recording, confirmed a trial, waited for actual cloud ASR, opened source audio, saved a separate correction and downloaded a ZIP Public HTTPS and real workers/storage; no customer media or purchase
Responsive browser 320/390/768/1440 workspace/review widths and 20 policy/checkout cases passed with zero page errors/overflow System Chromium; desktop/phone screenshots visually reviewed, not physical iPhone/Safari certification
Source lookup Real Crossref request returned DOI candidates; tests exercise malformed results/outage and route consent/ownership/rate limits Bibliographic matches only; no truth verdict or general search
Recovery/accounting Once-only reservation/settlement, partial/full refund, chargeback, outage, replay, ownership and revision cases passed Provider responses mocked; SQLite durable and concurrent checks real

Portfolio Seven DOM tests and four Chromium viewport checks passed for the updated card/link/details Sonaweft linked explicitly; Noteweld remains a proposal

The initial cloud probe exposed cross-environment exception/NumPy serialization failures; native JSON values and a plain error envelope fixed them before public enablement. Local testing found PyAV 19 incompatible with the pip speech dependency combination, so pip/cloud use the tested 15.1.0 pin. Nix supplies a separately tested compatible pair. The launcher also handled a Nix library-discovery SIGPIPE before release.

item.title: Custom domain and account access
item.description:
Public address: https://sonaweft.amirgomaa.com/ . A dedicated Cloudflare Workers Free gateway fronts the preserved Modal origin; processing, files and ledger remain on Modal. No paid provider plan, live checkout or new customer credentials are activated by this route. Reproducible shared code/config/tests are in the workspace at freelance/workflow/cloudflare-edge/.

The independent sonaweft-edge Modal secret authenticates short-lived client-IP assertions for existing quotas. Direct origin requests retain their previous proxy fallback. The gateway rejects unsafe foreign Origins before mapping its own Origin for upstream CSRF checks; CSRF tokens and host-only Secure/HttpOnly cookies remain enforced. Request/response bodies stream without document/audio buffering at the gateway. Cache mode is explicitly no-store; never use TTL zero as a cache-disable switch, because Cloudflare can strip session cookies when forcing caching.

item.title: Source workflow and diagnostics release
item.description:
Original record: Recording workflow, accounts and diagnostics — 18 October 2026.

Passage-to-quote follow-through — 19 October 2026

The listening toolbar can prepare reprocessing for its selected passage without re-uploading the recording or entering its original source timestamps manually. Clip-relative times are converted back to the original recording offset and quoted by the owned-upload endpoint. The reviewer must save an unsaved correction before preparing this quote. It defaults to transcription only; optional AI review remains a separate explicit choice and consent. No processing starts until confirmation. Earlier results and corrections remain separate.

item.title: Quality and cost measurement
item.description:
Offline scoring

scripts/score_quality.py compares human-prepared comparable text and observed measurements. It never uploads files, calls a model, spends credits or silently changes app limits. It reports exact character/word edit rates, not factual correctness or a calibrated confidence badge. Case, punctuation, numeric values, diacritics and technical symbols remain significant; only Unicode NFC and CRLF representation normalize. Whitespace splits word tokens, so CER is generally the more useful measure for languages without space-delimited words.

item.title: Declared image package inventory
item.description:
Actual CPU inspection of the current web/Whisper package images. Full metadata and license-file hashes , SHA256 4e1fbbab5b0c50ab0afd77f0c95341c011bd4829b23bc5a402661dfcda1a68a0. No model volume, app secret, customer source or GPU was used. The NVIDIA CUDA base image emitted its normal upstream notice on CPU; this is not GPU inference or a change to the desktop drivers.

These are Python distribution declarations and license-file hashes, not a complete license compatibility approval. Bundled native libraries, FFmpeg, system packages, the pinned CUDA image and model weights require their own exact terms. The actual ASR code pins Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3 revision edaa852ec7e145841d8ffdb056a99866b5f0a478; do not substitute current master terms.

item.title: Recoverable transcript review
item.description:
Sonaweft keeps the original machine transcript unchanged. Corrections and speaker labels are your annotations. Their latest 20 saved states now survive a reload or recovered workspace, for as long as the recording itself remains available.

Use saved history

  1. Open a completed result with Review & export.
  2. Expand Saved edit history and choose Load saved history.
  3. Choose a version. Changed passages show the current saved text/label beside the selected version. Reading history never replaces the editor draft.
  4. Save any unfinished correction or speaker label first. Select Restore this version as a new save and confirm the scope: every annotation in this result, rather than only the passage currently selected.
  5. Restoration creates a new revision. Retained earlier saves and the original ASR remain available; another tab cannot silently overwrite a newer revision.

The comparison is plain inert text, including source material that resembles HTML. The current save is marked explicitly. A result changed in another tab must be reopened before restoring; failed requests preserve the saved result and draft. Inputs are temporarily disabled during an annotation write to prevent lost typing. Refreshing listening/glossary cues preserves both drafts instead of resetting the editor, and a response for an earlier result cannot change the newly opened one.

item.title: The scientific recording example
item.description:
Listen to a real scientific explanation

The completed Sonaweft example is a continuous 63.65-second NOAA Ocean Podcast excerpt about why gravity varies across Earth. Megan Forbes interviews physicist Derek van Westrum in Understanding Gravity, episode 33 . The selected passage runs from 181.05 to 244.70 seconds in the source episode.

The example credits NOAA and the speakers, links the original source and states that no endorsement is implied. It is third-party source material, not an original recording made for this portfolio. The excerpt contains speech rather than a music insert; the reuse review is specific to this selected source.

item.title: Verified email and recovery
item.description:
Create and recover an account

Open Account to sign in with an existing passphrase. New email signup requests a link; explicitly choosing a passphrase on its confirmation form creates the credential. Opening a link alone does not create it. Existing unverified accounts can verify their address from their owned, recently authenticated workspace. Equal addresses never merge workspaces.

Verified addresses can request mailed resets. Completion revokes previous sessions and invalidates old recovery keys. Links expire after thirty minutes and work once; opening/previewing does not consume them. A separate saved key is optional when verified email recovery is available. Keep any key private.

item.title: From sources to connected notes
item.description:
Pageweft converts PDF pages to Markdown. Sonaweft transcribes recordings. Noteweld keeps editable notes, links, source material and portable vaults.

  1. Use Pageweft or Sonaweft, review the original against the result, and save any corrections.
  2. Download a fresh complete ZIP bundle from that application’s workspace.
  3. In Noteweld, open Source bundles, choose Pageweft or Sonaweft export, and validate the ZIP.
  4. Review its contents, confirm permission to retain them, and import. Notes and their original archive commit together. The original extraction, corrections and optional AI notes keep separate labels.
  5. Edit and link the imported notes. Download the original bundle or export a portable vault when needed.

The current Noteweld preview accepts an archive up to 4 MiB and 250 notes, subject to remaining account capacity. Pageweft can export fewer pages and omit the source PDF. A smaller recording gives a smaller Sonaweft bundle. Keep your own originals; a bundle includes source media only when the exporter includes it.
